diagnostic_evidence.quote: where $(e_{1}(x,u),e_{2}(x,u),u)$ is a positively oriented orthonomal basis of $\R^{3}$.

issues.failure_explanation: For a = f/|f|, b = a×u, c = u with u ⊥ f, one has det[a,b,c] = a·((a×u)×u) = -1, so the chosen triple is negatively oriented. The cylindrical τ formula requires a positively oriented basis, so e_2 should be u×f/|f|, and every cylindrical weight (α, γ_j) derived from this choice has the wrong sign.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace e_2 by u×f/|f| (equivalently flip the sign of γ_j / of the cylindrical component).
issues.overall_effect: The sign of the cylindrical component N(T)^{cyl} and of the weights γ_j in NC_delta/realembedding is flipped. Since the cylindrical component is orthogonal to the other components and the sign flip is applied uniformly, kernel inner products between two normal cycles are unaffected.
issues.title: Cylindrical basis (f/|f|, f/|f|×u, u) is negatively, not positively, oriented
issues.why_classification: A one-line local sign correction; no downstream metric value or guarantee changes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The cyclic coefficients $(a_{i}b_{j} - a_{j}b_{i})$ are nothing but the components of the cross product $e_{1}(x,u) \times e_{2}(x,u)$.

issues.failure_explanation: The coefficient of (0,e_1)∧(0,e_3) in the expansion is a_1b_3 − a_3b_1, whereas the second component of e_1×e_2 is u_2 = a_3b_1 − a_1b_3. Hence the correct coefficient is −u_2, not +u_2; the coefficient (a_ib_j − a_jb_i) is cyclic only for (i,j)=(2,3),(3,1),(1,2).

failure_location.quote: \tau_{x,u} = u_{1}\begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ e_2  \end{pmatrix}\wedge  \begin{pmatrix} 0\\ e_3 \end{pmatrix} + u_{2}\begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ e_1  \end{pmatrix}\wedge  \begin{pmatrix} 0\\ e_3 \end{pmatrix} + u_{3}\begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ e_1  \end{pmatrix}\wedge  \begin{pmatrix} 0\\ e_2 \end{pmatrix}

issues.overall_effect: The second coordinate of each spherical weight α_k (and of B(α_k)) has the wrong sign. Because the error is applied consistently to both shapes and the basis remains orthonormal, inner products ⟨α_k,α'_l⟩ = ⟨A_k,B_l⟩ and hence the metric are unaffected.
issues.title: Sign error in the e_1∧e_3 coefficient of the spherical τ_{x,u} expansion
issues.why_classification: Local sign correction with no effect on any metric value or guarantee.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: one may check the resulting scalar product of $N(\mathcal{T}),N(\mathcal{T}') \in W^{*}$ of \cref{NC_delta} agrees with \cref{NC_disc_met} derived in \cite{NCpaper}.

issues.failure_explanation: The component derivations give N^{cyl} = −(π/2)Σδ_{c_j}γ_j and N^{sph} = −πΣδ_{x_k}α_k. After absorbing the signs into γ_i, α_i, NC_delta assigns coefficient π to both terms (cylindrical should be π/2), while realembedding assigns π to the cylindrical term and π/2 to the spherical term (and evaluates the edge deltas at vertices x_i rather than edge centres c_j). Three mutually incompatible weightings are given. Moreover, with the derived orthonormal weights ⟨γ_j,γ'_l⟩ = ⟨f_j,g_l⟩⟨n_T,n_T'⟩ and ⟨α_k,α'_l⟩ = ⟨A_k,B_l⟩, none of the three versions reproduces NC_disc_met, which has π²/4 on both terms: the derived constants give π²/4 and π², NC_delta gives π² and π², realembedding gives π² and π²/4. The claimed agreement is therefore false as written. (Additionally, the quoted value ∫_C u dH¹(u) = (π/2)β_T for a unit half-circle is elementary computed as 2β_T, so the constants entering the cylindrical weight are themselves unreliable.)
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Recompute and fix the constants consistently (half-circle and hemisphere normal integrals, coefficients in NC_delta and realembedding, edge-centre locations c_j), and either verify agreement with NC_disc_met or correct the quoted discrete metric.
issues.overall_effect: The relative weighting of the edge (cylindrical) term versus the boundary (spherical) term is not a global scale but changes the shape metric; the functional actually compressed by Algorithm FunctionalCompressionAlg is not established to equal N(T) (as normalized in NC_disc_met), so the identification of compression error in V* with error to the normal cycle, and the metric used in the LDDMM experiments, are not consistent with the stated normal-cycle metric.
issues.title: Inconsistent π vs π/2 constants between the derived components, NC_delta and realembedding; claimed agreement with NC_disc_met fails
issues.why_classification: No new architecture is required, but the constants must be re-derived and the relative edge/boundary weighting fixed; the false agreement claim must be withdrawn or repaired, and the result remains recognizably the same Dirac-delta decomposition.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: which is a consistent approximation \cite{NCpaper}, as the edge-lengths tend to zero.

issues.failure_explanation: The only guarantee in the paper (thm:added-3) bounds the distance between the compressed functional and the discrete Dirac-delta functional built from the triangulation (itself an edge-centre approximation of N(T)). No bound relating this discrete functional to the normal cycle of the true underlying smooth shape is stated or proven; only qualitative consistency is cited. The conclusion claims a guarantee the paper does not establish.

failure_location.quote: our compression comes with fast error decay, and guarantees of small RKHS distance to the normal cycle of the true underlying shape.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the guarantee as controlling the RKHS distance to the discrete normal-cycle functional of the triangulation.
issues.overall_effect: The stated guarantee about the true underlying shape is unsupported; the actual guarantee concerns only the discrete target functional.
issues.title: Conclusion overclaims guarantees of RKHS distance to the normal cycle of the true underlying shape
issues.why_classification: A wording correction of scope; all formal results and the algorithm's actual guarantee are unaffected.
